question: A person travels one-third of a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h, and the remaining distance at a speed of 60 km/h. If he travels this distance at a uniform speed taking the same time, then what will be his speed (in km/h)?
solution:
Given:

A person travels one-third of a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h, and the remaining distance at a speed of 60 km/h. 

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Average speed = Total distance covered ÷ Total time taken

Calculation:

Let the distance be 3D km.

Time taken to complete one-third of a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h

⇒ (3D × 1/3) ÷ 45

⇒ D/45 hours

Remaining distance = 3D - D = 2D km

Time taken to complete remaining distance at a speed of 60 km/h

⇒ 2D ÷ 60

⇒ D/30 hours

Now, his speed will be = 3D over {{Dover 45} + {D over 30}}

⇒ 3 over {1 over 18} = 54 km/h

∴ His speed will be 54 km/h.
